ROLE: Release the reactor: close the owned epoll descriptor exactly once and free the loop object, leaving the borrowed broker and the borrowed listener descriptor untouched.

STRUCT.NAME: struct loop
STRUCT.ROLE: reactor being released; only epfd is a resource the loop owns

VAR.NAME: struct loop
VAR.ROLE: l->epfd is set to -1 after close so a repeated destroy cannot close a recycled descriptor number

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: close
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 on success, -1 with errno set (EBADF for an invalid descriptor, EINTR); the return value is deliberately ignored because a closed epoll descriptor has no state to flush
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: releases the descriptor the loop owns; the borrowing of l->broker and l->listener_fd ends with this call
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: close may report failure but the descriptor is released in every case except EINTR, where the process is exiting anyway and main() has already returned from loop_run

LOGIC.INPUT: l: the reactor returned by loop_create() and not yet destroyed (NULL tolerated).
LOGIC.ACTION: 1. If l == NULL return. 2. If l->epfd >= 0, call close(l->epfd) and set l->epfd = -1 (guarding against a repeated call). 3. free(l). The borrowed broker is not destroyed and the borrowed listener is not closed here: main() calls broker_destroy() and net_close_fd(&listener) afterwards, in that documented order.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: void. Afterwards no epoll descriptor created by loop_create() remains open and the loop object is released; the broker and all sessions (and the listener descriptor) are still alive and owned by the caller.
INVARIANTS_USED: the loop owns exactly one resource, its epoll descriptor; closing it drops every registration without touching the registered descriptors themselves
session and listener descriptors are owned by the broker, by session objects and by main, never by the loop
teardown order is loop_destroy() then the listener close then broker_destroy(), so no callback can run after the reactor is gone
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: loop_run() has returned and no further event dispatch will occur for this loop.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: l is released and no longer dereferenceable; the broker, its sessions and the listener descriptor are unchanged.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Called from the main thread after loop_run() returns; no concurrent access.

runtime: loop_create, loop_add_listener with a listening socket, one registered session fd
count open descriptors, loop_destroy(l), count again
